author: Staff reports, Foster's Daily Democrat
title: Dover students shine at 19th Poetry Out Loud competition - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff reports, Foster's Daily Democrat ,
1 days ago The Poetry Out Loud competition took place Dec. 19, marking its 19th year. The event celebrated nearly two decades of students bringing poetry to life on stage and showcased the expressive talent of Dover's young performers, according to a community announcement.
This year's competition crowned Jaden Mungdung as the winner for his performance of Gerard Manley Hopkins' "God's Grandeur." Mungdung previously earned third place with the same poem last year, highlighting his growth and stage presence.
Mungdung will represent Dover High School at the statewide Poetry Out Loud competition in Concord later this year. Second place was awarded to Rae Buchanon, and third place went to Gabriella Pezzino, both juniors. Other participants included Cat Duenas, Chase McNeil, Boden Sweet, Dannielynn Somers and Avery Bekkala.
The event also paid tribute to Ron Cole, a longtime judge and respected freelance writer who contributed for many years to Foster's Daily Democrat. Cole died earlier this year at the age of 84. Organizers and judges honored his dedication to the contest and his commitment to storytelling, journalism and the written word.
The event was coordinated by Lesley Hocking, a language arts teacher at Dover High School, according to the announcement. The panel of judges included Angela Carter, a marketing and communications specialist; Patty Falconer, deputy library director of the Dover Public Library; Jessica Purdy, a poet, author and professor at Southern New Hampshire University; and Sally Little, an English Department accuracy judge.
